headline: North-West account losses track directly with July's SLA breakdowns.
body: All the decline sits in North-West, where accounts dropped from 14 to 11 [E1]. That region also missed fulfilment SLA by 3.9%, and two enterprise accounts cited specific June delivery misses as their reason for leaving or pausing orders [E3]. A conveyor failure at warehouse WH-07 on June 25, combined with a picker shortage, is the operational root behind those SLA misses [E6]. Other regions show no delta, reinforcing that this is a localized North-West fulfilment issue, not a broad demand problem.

actions.driver: Fulfilment SLA misses tied to WH-07 breakdown
actions.action: Offer at-risk accounts a formal SLA guarantee now
actions.expected_impact: Reduce further churn among flagged enterprise accounts
actions.monitoring: Track weekly status of Meridian and Kalinga accounts

actions.driver: Fulfilment SLA misses tied to WH-07 breakdown
actions.action: Extend onboarding credits to accounts that paused orders
actions.expected_impact: Encourage resumption of paused order volume
actions.monitoring: Monitor order resumption rate over next 30 days

what_could_change: Confirmation that WH-07 throughput and staffing are fully restored would strengthen this conclusion further.
caveats: Evidence covers only two named accounts and one warehouse incident, so the sample is small.
